title: Beef Soup Stock (Brodo di Carne)
ingredients: 2 small, new carrots, or 1/2 of an old carrot
turkey leg (optional, to make stock richer)
1/2 pound of finely chopped beef (optional, to make stock richer)
steps: Boil the beef, bones, and vegetables in two quarts of water over a slow fire, adding pepper and salt.
Skim occasionally, and after two hours add two tablespoons of sherry.
Then strain through fine soup-strainer or cheese-cloth.
To make this stock richer, add a turkey leg to above receipt; boil one and a half hours, then add one-half a pound of finely chopped beef, cook for half an hour longer, then strain.
To make meat jelly, add a little gelatine to the soup stock five minutes before straining.

title: Chicken Broth (Brodo di Capone)
steps: This is made like the meat stock, substituting a fowl in place of the beef and bones.

title: Rice Soup (Minestra di Riso)
steps: Cover the rice with water and boil for ten minutes.
Drain and add to the stock (after it has been strained).
Boil for five or ten minutes more.

title: Stracciatella Soup (Minestra di Stracciatella)
steps: Beat the egg, yolk and white together.
Add salt, the cheese grated, and the bread crumbs; mix well together.
Add to the boiling stock (strained).
Stir well with a fork to prevent the egg from setting, and boil for four or five minutes.

title: Vegetable Chowder (Minestrone alla Milanese)
ingredients: 2 slices of lean pork (or a ham bone)
1 tablespoon of peas, fresh or canned
steps: Put into the stock the slices of pork, cut into small pieces; or, if desired, a ham bone may be substituted for the pork.
Add the tomatoes, cut into small pieces also, the onions, in small pieces, and the rice.
Boil all together until the rice is cooked.
Then add the beans and the peas and cook a little longer.
The soup is ready when it is thick.

title: Fish Broth (Brodo di Pesce)
ingredients: 1 liberal pound of fresh codfish, or any other lean fish for boiling
steps: Boil until fish is thoroughly cooked.
Strain and serve.

title: Codfish Soup (Zuppa di Merluzzo)
ingredients: 4 tablespoons of good olive-oil, plus 1/2 tablespoon more
2 tomatoes, skinned and with seeds removed, cut into slices
1 medium-sized potato, peeled and cut into slices
steps: Take one-half pound of salt codfish that has been soaked, cut it up into squares, but not small.
Prepare in a saucepan four tablespoons of good olive-oil, and one small onion cut into pieces.
Cook the onion in the oil over a slow fire, without allowing the onion to become colored, then add a small bunch of parsley stems, a small piece of celery, a bay-leaf, and a small sprig of thyme.

Cool for a few moments, then add two tomatoes, skinned and with the seeds removed, and cut into slices, two tablespoons of dry white wine, and one medium-sized potato, peeled and cut into slices, and, lastly, one cup of water.
When the potato is half cooked, add the codfish, then one-half tablespoon more of olive-oil.
Remove the parsley stems, and put in instead one-half tablespoon of chopped-up parsley; add a good pinch of pepper, and some salt, if needed.
When the vegetables are thoroughly cooked pour the soup over pieces of toasted or fried bread, and serve.

title: Lentil Soup (Brodo di Lenticchie)
steps: Cover the lentils with water and boil until they are quite soft.
Pass them through a colander or a sieve.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, add the lentils and cream, mixing well.
Add a ladleful of the stock, and boil for a few minutes; then add the rest of the desired amount of stock, a ladleful at a time.

title: Vegetable Soup (Zuppa alla Primaverile)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon of tomato paste (or 1 tomato, peeled and cut into small pieces)
steps: Take some cabbage, carrots, celery, onions, turnips, lettuce, squash, potatoes, beans, and peas. Chop each into very small pieces, wash and drain.
Take a saucepan, put in a heaping tablespoon of butter; chop up another small piece of onion and add to butter and fry until onion is golden.
Then add all the vegetables, salt, and pepper, and cover the saucepan.

When the vegetables are half cooked, and their juice has become absorbed, dissolve one tablespoon of tomato paste in one-third of a cup of hot water, and add. (Instead of the tomato paste there may be added to the onion, before putting in the vegetables, one tomato, peeled and cut into small pieces; when the tomato is cooked add the vegetables.)
Then add water, a little at a time, until you have sufficient quantity for two persons.
Take a slice of bread and cut into small squares or diamonds—toast or fry as desired—put these into the soup plates, and pour the soup (without straining) over them.

title: Lettuce Soup (Zuppa di Lattuga)
ingredients: The leaves of a head of celery
2 tablespoons of peas, fresh or canned
a little cold stock or water
steps: Put the potatoes, cold boiled, into the stock when it boils.
Add the celery leaves, the lettuce chopped up, the peas, and the flour mixed well with a little cold stock or water.
Boil for one hour and a half, and serve with little squares of fried bread.

title: Pumpkin Soup (Zuppa di Zucca)
steps: Peel the pumpkin and remove the seeds, cut into small pieces, and put into a saucepan with the butter, the sugar, a pinch of salt, and the water.
Boil for two hours.
Drain and put back into the saucepan with the milk, which has been boiled.
Allow it to come to a boil, and then serve it with squares of fried bread.

title: Potato Soup (Zuppa alla Provinciale)
steps: Boil the potatoes, then rub them through a sieve.
Put them into a saucepan with the butter, a little salt, and the cream or milk.
Simmer until it is thick, then add the yolks of the two eggs to form it into a paste.
Turn out onto the bread-board, cut into small dice, and throw them into the stock, which must be boiling.
If desired, before serving sprinkle a little Parmesan cheese into the soup.

title: Ravioli with Brains
steps: Take one lamb's brains and parboil in slightly salted water for five minutes.
Put into a bowl with a small quantity of curds, one egg, salt and pepper, dash of nutmeg, and a little grated Parmesan cheese, and mix all together.
Then put by teaspoonfuls on the paste as in preceding receipt.
Cook for ten minutes in boiling salted water, and serve with tomato sauce.

title: Ravioli of Curds and Spinach
steps: Cook the spinach, drain, and chop up fine.
Add the curds, one egg, salt and pepper, dash of nutmeg, and a little grated cheese.
Add to the paste, and boil as before.

title: Sweet Ravioli (Ravioli Dolce)
steps: Work the flour, 1 tablespoon of butter, and 2 tablespoons of lard into a paste and roll out thin.
Take one-half pound of curds, add one egg, and the yolk of a second egg, two tablespoons of granulated sugar, a few drops of extract of vanilla.
Mix well together and add to the paste as before.
Then fry in lard until a golden brown.
Serve with powdered sugar.

title: Timbale of Macaroni
ingredients: 5 tablespoons of hot water (or equal quantity of tomato sauce without water)
steps: Chop up fine together a small piece of ham fat, one-half of onion, piece of celery, parsley, and small piece of carrot.
Put into a saucepan, and when the vegetables are fried add two or three mushrooms which have been chopped fine.
After five minutes add two tablespoons of tomato paste, thinned with five tablespoons of hot water (or equal quantity of tomato sauce without water).
When the sauce is cooked take out the mushrooms and put them on one side.
Take one-half pound of macaroni, boil in salted water for fifteen minutes, drain, and add the sauce described above, along with two tablespoons Parmesan cheese, grated, and one tablespoon of butter.
Butter well a mold, then cover with a thin layer of bread crumbs the bottom and sides.
Pour into the mold one-half the macaroni, then place on it a layer of mushrooms which you have taken out of the sauce.
Now add the other half of the macaroni, and then another thin layer of bread crumbs.
Put the mold into the oven without turning it over, and bake in a slow oven until well browned. Then turn out and serve.

title: Rice Timbale
steps: Make in the same way as the preceding one (Timbale of Macaroni), only substituting rice for macaroni, using one-half cup of rice.

title: Timbale of Ribbon Macaroni
steps: Prepare as the two preceding ones, using Ribbon Macaroni instead of rice or ordinary macaroni.

title: Rice with Peas
ingredients: 1 can of green peas (or fresh peas)
steps: Chop the onion up fine and put it into the saucepan with one-half the butter (one tablespoon).
Cook until the onion is brown, then pour on the rice (raw) and fry until the rice is dry.
Add hot water, a ladleful at a time, taking care not to let the rice boil too hard, as it will then become hard in the middle and floury around the edges.
When the rice is cooked, put the saucepan at the back of the stove, and add the rest of the butter.

Prepare the peas by chopping a small piece of ham fat, one-half small onion, and some parsley together fine, adding three tablespoons of olive-oil, salt, and pepper, and putting into a saucepan on the fire.
When the onion is colored add one can of green peas (or fresh peas).
When the peas have absorbed all the olive-oil add a sufficient quantity of broth to cover them (or water) and cook until peas are soft.
Before taking off the stove add a little grated Parmesan cheese and the prepared peas to the rice, mix with one tablespoon of Parmesan cheese, and serve.

title: Rice "alla Romana" (Risotto alla Romana)
ingredients: 1 tablespoon of red or white wine
1 tablespoon of tomato paste (or 2 and 1/2 tablespoons of other tomato sauce)
rice (a little less than a cupful)
steps: Chop the ham fat, celery, parsley, lean beef, onion, and mushrooms together and put them into a large saucepan with a small piece of butter.
Cook until the meat is well browned.
Add one tablespoon of red or white wine and cook for a few minutes.
Add one tablespoon of tomato paste dissolved in a little hot water, or two and one-half tablespoons of the other tomato sauce.
Cook well, adding from time to time a little water—one-half cup in all.
Wash the rice, add it to the other ingredients in the saucepan, and cook for about twenty minutes, until the rice is soft, adding more water from time to time.
Add two tablespoons of grated Parmesan cheese, mix well, and serve, with more cheese if desired.

title: Risotto "alla Nostrale"
ingredients: 1 and 1/2 tablespoons of tomato paste (or 2 tablespoons of other tomato sauce)
steps: Take a small piece of onion, slice into small bits, and put into a saucepan with two tablespoons of butter. Cook until onion is browned.
Wash well one-half cup of rice. Put it into the saucepan with the onion, add salt and pepper, and fry until the rice is dry.
Take one and one-half tablespoons of tomato paste, thinned with hot water (or two tablespoons of other tomato sauce), and add to the rice.
Little by little add hot water until the rice is cooked through (about one cup of hot water).
Add grated cheese, Parmesan or Gruyère, one and one-half tablespoons of butter, and mix well over the fire, then serve.

title: Rice with Butter and Cheese (Riso in Bianco)
steps: Take one-half cup of rice and boil in salted water.
After twenty minutes of boiling take off the fire and drain.
Put the rice back into a saucepan with three tablespoons of grated cheese (Parmesan) and three tablespoons of butter.
Mix well and serve as an entrée, or around a plate of meat.

title: Rice with Tomatoes
ingredients: strained juice and pulp of 7 or 8 tomatoes
steps: Boil a cup of rice soft in hot water, shaking it now and then without stirring.
Drain it, add a little milk in which a beaten egg has been mixed, one teaspoon of butter, and a little pepper and salt.
Simmer for five minutes, and if the rice has not absorbed all the milk, drain it again.
Put the rice around a dish, smooth it into a wall, wash it over with the yolk of a beaten egg, and put it into the oven until firm.
Take the strained juice and pulp of seven or eight tomatoes, season with pepper, a little salt and sugar, and one-half of a chopped-up onion.
Stew for twenty minutes, then stir in one tablespoon of butter and two tablespoons of fine bread crumbs.
Stew three or four minutes to thicken, and then pour the tomatoes into the dish, in the middle of the rice, and serve.

title: Rice with Tomatoes "all' Indiana"
steps: Wash a cup of rice and boil it.
Take seven or eight good-sized tomatoes, boil and strain them, and season with salt and a little allspice.
Take a baking-dish and put into it alternate layers of tomato and rice, finishing off with a layer of tomato, covered up with grated bread crumbs moistened with melted butter.
Bake in a moderate oven for a good half-hour.

title: Roux for Sauces
ingredients: stock or milk (one cup for every tablespoon of butter or flour)
steps: Put one tablespoon of flour and one of butter into a saucepan and cook until the flour has lost any raw taste.
Then put the saucepan on the back of the stove and add slowly the stock or milk, one cup for every tablespoon of butter or flour, and stir until smooth.
For white sauces take care the flour does not color; for dark sauces let it brown, but take care it does not burn.

title: Agro Dolce Sauce
steps: Mix well together and let soak for two hours.
Pour it over venison or veal, and simmer for ten minutes.

title: Béchamel Sauce No. 1
steps: Put two ounces of butter and two tablespoons of flour into a saucepan and stir for five minutes.
Pour one and one-half pints of boiling milk gradually in, beating well with a whisk.
Add some nutmeg, a few peppercorns, a pinch of salt, and some chopped mushrooms.
Cook for one-quarter of an hour, and rub through a fine sieve.

title: Béchamel Sauce No. 2
steps: Mix three tablespoons of butter and three of flour to a smooth paste, put some peppercorns, one-half an onion, one-half a carrot sliced, a small piece of mace, two teacups of white stock, a pinch of salt and of grated nutmeg, in a stew-pan.
Simmer for one-half an hour, stirring often.
Add one teacup of cream; boil at once, and strain and serve.

title: Tomato Sauce No. 1
ingredients: 1 heaping tablespoon butter (or 1/2 tablespoon of good lard)
steps: Take ten fresh tomatoes, remove the skins, cut them up; put them into a saucepan and boil them until soft.
Then pass them through a sieve.
Put their juice into a saucepan with one heaping tablespoon of butter or one-half tablespoon of good lard, salt and pepper, and boil again, adding water if the sauce becomes too thick.

title: Tomato Sauce No. 2
ingredients: a few leaves of sweet basil
steps: Mince one-quarter of an onion, one-half a stalk of celery, a few leaves of sweet basil, and a bunch of parsley up fine.
Add one-half cup of olive-oil, a pinch of salt and one of pepper, and cut eight or nine tomatoes into slices.
Boil until the sauce is as thick as cream, stirring occasionally, then strain through a sieve and serve.

title: Tomato Sauce No. 3
steps: Take four pounds of tomatoes, cut them in two, and put them into a two-quart saucepan with two wineglasses of water, two saltspoons of salt, one of pepper, cover the saucepan, and boil for forty minutes, stirring often to prevent burning; then strain.
Make a roux in another saucepan with one ounce of butter and three-quarters of an ounce of flour.
Cook for three minutes, mixing well.
Take roux off the fire, and pour the tomatoes into it a little at a time, stirring to keep it smooth.
Add two wineglasses of stock, put on the fire, and cook for twenty minutes, stirring all the time.

title: Butter Sauce
steps: Stir with a wooden spoon over the fire until the butter is half melted, then take it off and continue to stir until it is quite liquid.

title: Lombarda Sauce
steps: Put two tumblers of white roux and one of chicken jelly into a saucepan, reduce, and add three yolks of eggs mixed with two ounces of butter and the juice of one-half lemon.
Before it boils take the saucepan off the fire, and add one tumbler of thick tomato sauce, strain, and just before serving add one tablespoon of sweet herbs minced fine.

title: "Alla Panna" Sauce
steps: Melt one-half a pound of butter, add a little flour, salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg.
Stir until thick, then add one pint of cream, a little chopped parsley, and heat for five minutes.

title: Meat Sauce
steps: Put into a saucepan one pound of beef and one-half an onion chopped up with three ounces of lard, some parsley, salt, pepper, one clove, and a very small slice of ham.
Fry these over a hot fire for a few moments, moving them continually, and when the onion is browned add four tablespoons of red wine, and four tablespoons of tomato sauce (or tomato paste).
When this sauce begins to sputter, add, little by little, some boiling water.
Stick a fork into the meat from time to time to allow the juices to escape.

Take a little of the sauce in a spoon, and when it looks a good golden color, and there is a sufficient quantity to cover the meat, put the covered saucepan at the back of the stove and allow it to simmer until the meat is thoroughly cooked.
Then take out the meat, slice it, prepare macaroni, or any paste you desire, and serve it with the meat, and the sauce poured over all, and the addition of butter and grated cheese.

title: Economical Sauce
steps: Take one-half of an old onion and chop it up fine. Take one small carrot, wash it, scrape it, and cut it into transverse slices; do the same with a stalk of celery, some parsley, and one fresh or canned mushroom.
Then take a slice of ham (raw if possible), fat and lean, about four fingers wide and one finger high. Chop it up fine, and put it into a medium-sized saucepan with one tablespoon of butter.

When the ham is colored, put in the chopped-up vegetables, one clove, salt, and pepper, and stir constantly, allowing the vegetables to cook thoroughly but not to burn. It should be a golden color. A little red wine may be added if you have it.
Then add four fresh tomatoes, cut into several pieces, the skins removed, and the seeds taken out.

Allow these to cook in the sauce until they sputter, then add a little water (or bouillon if you have it), allow it to boil for a few moments more, then take it off the fire and pass it through a sieve or fine colander, pressing hard so that all will pass through.
If it is too thick after straining, add water or bouillon, and put it back and allow it to boil again a few moments.

title: Hot Piquante Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup bouillon (or water in which you have dissolved 1 tablespoon of extract of beef)
steps: Chop up fine two ounces of lean ham and a small piece of onion, add a little celery, the stalks of parsley, one clove, one-half tablespoon of pepper, and one-half bay-leaf.
Pour over these ingredients a scant one-half cup of vinegar.
Cover the saucepan and allow it to boil until it has consumed one-half.
Put into another saucepan one-half cup of bouillon (or water in which you have dissolved one tablespoon of extract of beef).
Allow it to boil, and then thicken with a teaspoon of potato flour which has been diluted in a little cold water.
Drop this, little by little, into the saucepan until you have gained the required thickness for the sauce.
Then pour in the boiled vinegar, passing it through cheese-cloth.
Mix well together and add a teaspoon of French mustard, some capers, and some chopped-up pickles.
Serve hot with meats or tongue. The pepper should predominate in this sauce.

title: Piquante Sauce with Egg
steps: Take some anchovy paste, two tablespoons of chopped parsley, some capers and chopped pickles, one teaspoon of French mustard, and the yolks of two hard-boiled eggs.
Work this all together into a paste, then add three tablespoons of olive-oil and two or three of vinegar and a pinch of salt and pepper.
This sauce is good with both meat and fish.

title: Eggs with Peas
steps: Take one and one-half cups of green peas, and cook them with one and one-half tablespoons of good butter, and a pinch of salt.
Take four hard-boiled eggs, cut them in two lengthwise, and put them on a platter; pour over them the peas as a sauce.

title: Eggs "alla Milanese"
ingredients: Cream of Lemon Sauce (1 cup cold water, 1 tablespoon starch, 1 heaping tablespoon powdered sugar, 1 cup milk, pinch of salt, grated lemon-rind, 2 yolks of eggs)
steps: Hard boil four eggs, cut them in four pieces each, put them in a platter, and pour over them the following sauce:

Cream of Lemon Sauce: Take one cup of cold water, and pour one-half of it in a bowl with one tablespoon of starch, stir well until starch is dissolved. Pour the other one-half onto one heaping tablespoon of powered sugar and boil for a few moments—until sugar is thoroughly dissolved. Allow it to cool, and then add the starch, and one cup of milk, a pinch of salt, a little grated lemon-rind, and two yolks of eggs. Mix all thoroughly, then strain through a sieve, then put on the stove again, and over a moderate fire, stir it constantly, always in the same direction, until it has assumed the thickness you desire.

title: Eggs "alla Sciarmante"
steps: Hard boil four eggs; cut into several pieces.
Boil down to a syrup one heaping tablespoon of sugar, rind of one-quarter of lemon, one scant cup of water, and a little piece of cinnamon.
Then remove the lemon-rind and the cinnamon, and add one cup of milk or cream.
When heated through, take off of fire, and add the yolks of four eggs, beating well together.
Then pour the sauce over the hard-boiled eggs in a shallow baking-dish, put it in a very moderate oven, and bake.
Before serving squeeze on a little lemon juice and garnish with squares of fried bread.

title: Eggs with Piquante Sauce
steps: Chop up fine one pickled pepper, one teaspoon of capers, one-half small pickled onion and one pickle, and some parsley.
Dissolve in boiling water one tablespoon of butter, add the juice of one-half of lemon, a pinch of flour to give a little body, and the chopped pickles. If too sour add some sugar.
Hard boil four eggs, cut them in four, and pour over them the sauce.

title: Eggs "alla Monachile"
steps: Hard boil four eggs, divide them in half, and pour over them the following sauce:

Put two tablespoons of vinegar into a saucepan and one tablespoon of sugar (brown or white), fifteen almonds chopped up fine, and a small piece of candied citron. Let it boil for a little while, then add a pinch of cinnamon, cloves, pepper, and salt, and if too acid add a little water.
Before taking off the stove add a little flour to give body to the sauce. Pour over the eggs and serve.

title: Eggs "alla Fiorentina"
steps: Hard boil four eggs. Let them cool in a bowl of cold water. Peel them and divide them in half.
Take the yolks and mix with them one heaping tablespoon of butter, one tablespoon of Parmesan cheese grated, and a little salt and pepper.
Put this mixture into a saucepan with the yolks of two raw eggs, and one-half of the white of one egg. Stir well until the mixture becomes thick.
Then fill the hard-boiled whites of the eggs with the stuffing; if any stuffing remains over, spread it on the platter under the eggs.
Then put one-half cup of milk in a saucepan with one-half tablespoon of butter and one-half tablespoon of flour, salt, and pepper.
Boil for a few moments, stirring well, then pour over the eggs, sprinkle well with grated Parmesan cheese, and put in the oven and brown.

title: Lightning Omelette
ingredients: slices of stale bread (brown bread is better than white)
very thin slices of Gruyère cheese
steps: Butter a baking-dish and put in the bottom of it slices of stale bread (brown bread is better than white) which have been dipped in milk.
Then put in a layer of very thin slices of Gruyère cheese.
Take two eggs, beat them up to a froth, add salt and pepper, pour them into a baking-dish on top of the bread and cheese, then put it in the oven until it is browned on top. Serve hot.

title: Eggs "alla Piacentina"
ingredients: very thin slices of cheese, Parmesan or Gruyère
steps: Take the whites of four eggs, and beat until stiff.
Then add the yolks and one rounded tablespoon of melted butter, and a little salt and pepper.
Take a small baking-dish, butter it well, and put in the bottom a layer or two of very thin slices of cheese, Parmesan or Gruyère.
Put into the oven for a few moments until thoroughly heated, then pour on the whites of eggs mixed with the other ingredients, put back in the oven, and serve when the eggs are a golden brown.

title: Eggs "alla Benedettina"
steps: Roast two small peppers, take off their skins, remove the seeds, and cut into strips.
Take two tomatoes (not too ripe), boil them, remove the skins and seeds, and cut into thin strips also.
Then wash two anchovies, remove the bones, and cut also into strips.
Take a small baking-dish, put in the strips of peppers and tomatoes and the anchovies.
Add two tablespoons of good olive-oil and put on the top of the stove until the ingredients boil.
Then break into the dish four eggs, taking care to keep the yolks whole. Add salt and pepper, and put the dish into the oven until the eggs are cooked.

title: Eggs "alla Romana"
ingredients: Meat Sauce (ham fat, onion, celery, carrot, parsley, small piece of beef, 1 and 1/2 tablespoons red or white wine, 1 tablespoon tomato paste diluted with water or 4 fresh tomatoes)
steps: Beat four eggs, whites and yolks together. Add one tablespoon of milk or cream, salt and pepper, one tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese, and a little chopped-up parsley.
With this make three or four omelettes about the thickness of a ten-cent piece.
As the omelettes are finished lay them on a napkin to cool; then cut them transversely into strips about one-quarter of an inch wide.
Then put the strips into a saucepan with some heated butter. Heat them through thoroughly and serve with grated cheese and the following meat sauce poured over them:

Meat Sauce: Chop up some ham fat with a little onion, celery, carrot, and parsley. Add a small piece of beef and cook until beef is well colored. Then add one and one-half tablespoons of red wine (or white), cook until wine is absorbed, then add one tablespoon of tomato paste diluted with water, or four fresh tomatoes, and boil fifteen minutes.

title: Codfish "alla Giardiniera"
steps: Take one pound of salted codfish, boil it, remove the skin and bones, and shred it.
Take one good carrot, one-half a turnip, scrape them, cut them into slices, and boil them for a few moments.
Drain off the water, and put them into a saucepan with one and one-half tablespoons of butter and finish cooking them, adding from time to time a little boiling water.
When the vegetables are cooked add the codfish, mix well, and serve.

title: Codfish with Egg Sauce
steps: Take one pound of salt codfish, boil it, and remove the skin and bones.
Fry lightly in butter, adding chopped-up parsley, salt, and pepper.
Stir about constantly, and add from time to time a little boiling water, until the fish is thoroughly cooked.
Beat up the yolks of two eggs and add them with a little flour, and cook for a few moments more.
Squeeze on some lemon juice and serve.

title: Codfish "alla Marinaia"
steps: Take one pound of salt codfish. Boil slightly until you can remove the skin and bones.
Chop up fine a piece of onion, and parsley, and fry them in a saucepan with three tablespoons of best olive-oil.
Put in the codfish with salt, pepper, and a pinch of allspice.
While this is cooking, put into another saucepan three tablespoons of best vinegar, two tablespoons of fish broth, and one-half bay-leaf.
Add a little flour to give body to the sauce, stir well, then remove the bay-leaf, and take the saucepan off the fire.
Arrange the platter with pieces of fried bread in a layer on the bottom, then the codfish, and then the sauce poured over it.

title: Fresh Codfish "al Vino Bianco"
ingredients: 3-quarters of a pound of fresh codfish
steps: Remove the bones from three-quarters of a pound of fresh codfish and cut into slices lengthwise.
Butter a baking-dish, put in the fish, put more butter on top of it, salt and pepper, and one-half glass of dry white wine.
Cook for twenty minutes in a hot oven.
Place the fish on a platter, take the juice left over in the baking-dish, put it into a saucepan, add a little flour, some more butter, and the juice of half a lemon.
Before taking off the fire, add some chopped-up parsley, and then pour the sauce over the fish, and serve.

title: Codfish with Green Peppers
steps: Take one-half pound of salted codfish which has been soaked to remove the saltiness.
Remove the skin and bones, and cut the codfish into small squares.
Dip it again into fresh water, and put the squares onto a napkin to dry. (The fish may either be left as it is, or before proceeding, you may roll it in flour and fry it in lard or oil.)
Take two good-sized green peppers, roast them on top of the stove, remove the skins and seeds, wash them, dry them, and cut them in narrow strips.
Put three generous tablespoons of olive-oil into a saucepan with one onion cut up small, and fry the onion over a slow fire.
Take two big tomatoes, skin them, remove the seeds and hard parts, and cut them into small pieces.
When the onion has taken a good color, add the tomatoes, and cook until they sputter, then add the peppers and a little salt and pepper. If the sauce is too thick add a little water.
When the peppers are half cooked, add some chopped-up parsley and the codfish. Cover up the saucepan and let it simmer until the fish is cooked.

title: Onions "alla Parmegiana"
steps: Take six onions. Take out the centers with an apple-corer and fill them up with the following stuffing: One tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese mixed with two hard-boiled eggs and chopped parsley.
Boil them first, then roll them in flour and fry them in olive-oil or butter.
Put them in a baking-dish with one-half tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese and one tablespoon of melted butter.
Put them in the oven and bake until golden.

title: Onions "alla Veneziana"
steps: Take six small onions, remove the centers with an apple-corer. Boil them for a few moments, drain them, and stuff them with the following:

Take a piece of bread, dip it in milk, squeeze out the milk, and mix the bread with one tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese, the yolks of two hard-boiled eggs. Mix well together, then add some fine-chopped parsley, a pinch of sugar, salt and pepper, and the yolk of one raw egg; mix again well.
Stuff the onions with the mixture, dip them in flour and in egg, and fry them in lard.

Make a piquante sauce as follows: Chop up fine some pickles, capers, and pickled pepper, and add one-half cup of water. When these are cooked, add one tablespoon of butter and cook a little while longer.
Put the onions on a platter, pour the sauce over them and serve.

title: Lima Beans with Ham
ingredients: 3-quarters of a pound of lima beans
steps: Take three-quarters of a pound of lima beans, very tender young ones. Put them in boiling water for about five minutes to whiten them.
Put into a saucepan one heaping tablespoon of butter, some chopped parsley, and one small onion chopped up fine.
When the onion is fried, add three ounces of raw ham, also chopped up.
When the ham is fried put in the lima beans, and a little while before they are cooked add two or three tablespoons of stock.
Serve with dice of fried bread.

title: Fried Squash, Parsnips, Celery, and Mushrooms
steps: Take two small squash, the smallest size possible; cut off the two ends, divide them in two, and slice them in fine slices lengthwise. Put them in an earthen dish and sprinkle well with salt.
Take one parsnip, scrape it, wash it, and boil it slightly, slice it, add it to the squash with more salt.
Take the heart of celery, boil for a moment, and slice as with the other vegetables.
Lastly, take some mushrooms, not very large ones, clean them, boil them a moment, and add them to the rest.
Dry all the vegetables with a clean towel, mix them all together, roll them thoroughly in flour, dip in egg, and fry in hot lard, dropping them in carelessly.
Serve them in a hot dish with a napkin under them.

title: Pumpkin "alla Parmegiana"
ingredients: thin slices of cheese (Parmesan or Gruyère)
steps: Take a slice of pumpkin, remove the rind and the seeds, cut into square pieces, and then slice these into slivers about the thickness of a ten-cent piece.
Boil these for a moment in salted water, drain and put them into a saucepan, and fry in butter, with a little salt and a pinch of allspice.

Serve with grated Parmesan cheese and melted butter. Or, if preferred, when the pumpkin is fried, put it in a baking-dish, add thin slices of cheese (Parmesan or Gruyère), and put it into the oven until browned.

title: Fried Pumpkin
steps: Take a slice of pumpkin, remove the rind and the seeds. Cut it into strips as for French fried potatoes, only finer.
Roll in flour and dip in egg, and fry in boiling lard or olive-oil.
If desired as garnishing for meat, cut the pumpkin exceedingly fine, roll in flour, but not in egg, and fry.

title: Spinach "alla Romana"
steps: Clean and prepare the spinach.
Put one pint of cold water with one tablespoon of salt on to boil, and when it boils put in the spinach.
When the spinach is cooked—in about ten minutes—drain it in a colander, and turn onto it the cold water from the faucet for a few moments.
Squeeze out all the water with the hands.
Put three tablespoons of olive-oil into a frying-pan; when this is thoroughly hot add the spinach, salt, and pepper.
Cook for a few moments, stirring well with a fork and spoon, so the oil will permeate the spinach; then serve. Do not chop the spinach.

title: Hot Wine
ingredients: one pint of red or white wine
piece of rind of lemon or orange
steps: Put into the saucepan one pint of red or white wine, the first preferred.
Add two heaping tablespoons of sugar, a piece of rind of lemon or orange, and a small stick of cinnamon.
Put it onto the fire and stir until the sugar is dissolved.
When the wine boils, strain it through some cheese-cloth and pour it into glasses, and serve hot.

title: Milk of Almond Ice
steps: Take one-half pound of almonds. Remove the shells and skins, and put them into a large receptacle of cold water.
Add three bitter almonds to the number.
Remove them from the water, and pound them up in a bowl, adding from time to time a little water.
Then add more water and put them into a cheese-cloth and wring it, to extract all the juices you can.
Then pound them some more, adding water, and squeeze out as before.
To the milk you have extracted from the almonds add four tablespoons of powdered sugar and one-half tablespoon of orange water; put into the freezer and freeze.
If desired, you can put half the quantity of almonds and the other half of cantaloup seeds, pound together, and proceed in the same manner.

title: Macaroni with Tomato Sauce (Maccheroni al Sugo)
ingredients: celery length of a finger (alternative sauce)
7 or 8 tomatoes, fresh or canned (alternative sauce)
steps: Boil water in a properly sized saucepan, add salt, break macaroni, cover, and boil for 15 minutes.
Prepare the sauce by finely chopping ham fat, onion, celery, and parsley together.
Cook the chopped mixture in a frying-pan until grease is colored, adding a small lump of butter if desired.
Dissolve tomato paste in a little hot water, add to the pan, and boil together for 15 minutes.

Alternatively, if no tomato paste is available, make sauce by cooking finely chopped onion, celery, basil-leaves, parsley, sliced tomatoes, salt, pepper, and olive-oil until thick like cream, then strain.
Drain macaroni, add to the frying-pan with the sauce, mix well with a fork and spoon over heat, add grated Parmesan cheese, mix again, and serve.

title: Macaroni with Meat and Sauce (Maccheroni al sugo di Carne)
ingredients: 1/2 pound beef without fat (or veal or mutton)
steps: Prepare the ham fat chopped with onion, celery, and parsley.
Cut the meat into several pieces and place in a frying-pan with the fat mixture, salt, and pepper.
Cook until the meat is colored, then add wine and allow it to be absorbed.
Add tomato paste dissolved in hot water, cover, and boil together for 5 minutes.
Add 1 cup of boiling water and simmer until the meat is thoroughly cooked, about half an hour.
Boil and strain the macaroni, pour the meat sauce over it, mix well, and serve with the meat in the center, macaroni around it, and sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Macaroni with Butter and Cheese (Maccheroni al Burro)
steps: Boil and drain the macaroni.
Add table-butter and grated Parmesan cheese to the macaroni in the saucepan.
Mix well over the fire and serve.

title: Sicilian Macaroni with Eggplant
steps: Slice the eggplant, place under a weighted plate to extract bitter juices, then fry delicately in lard.
Make a ragout by frying chickens' hearts and livers in butter in a saucepan, then add tomato paste thinned with hot water and cook for 15 minutes.
Boil and drain the macaroni, place in the saucepan with the hearts and livers, add eggplant and grated Parmesan cheese, mix well together, and serve.

title: Vermicelli with Olive-oil and Anchovies
steps: Boil vermicelli in salted water and drain.
Cut up fine three anchovies and fry them in a saucepan with olive-oil.
Add the vermicelli to the saucepan, mix well on the fire for a few moments, and serve.

title: Vermicelli with Olive-oil, Olives, Capers, and Anchovies
steps: Cook vermicelli in well-salted water for about ten minutes.
Fry finely cut anchovies, olives, and capers in olive-oil in a saucepan.
Add well-drained vermicelli, mix well, place the saucepan at the back of the stove, and turn with a fork every few minutes until thoroughly cooked.

title: Vermicelli with Fish
steps: Boil vermicelli in salted water, drain, mix with olive-oil and parsley, and set aside to cool.
Split smelts, remove bones, and fry slightly in olive-oil.
Butter a baking pan, sprinkle with bread crumbs, and layer half of the cold vermicelli inside.
Pour over a thick tomato sauce made by cooking tomato paste in olive-oil.
Add the smelts cut in two, some anchovy, capers, chopped olives, and mushroom.
Add the remaining tomato sauce, the second half of the vermicelli, and top with a layer of bread crumbs, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook in a moderate oven for about an hour and a quarter, adding olive-oil as needed to prevent drying.

title: Spaghetti with Tunny-fish
steps: Boil spaghetti in salted water.
Cut tunny-fish into small pieces and fry in a saucepan in its own oil (add an extra tablespoon of olive-oil if needed).
Add chopped parsley, peeled and deseeded tomatoes, and pepper, letting the tomatoes cook thoroughly.
Add the cooked spaghetti to the saucepan, mix thoroughly with the sauce and tunny using a fork and spoon, and serve.

title: Timbale of Vermicelli with Tomatoes (Neapolitan Receipt)
steps: Cut tomatoes in two crosswise and layer in a baking-dish, alternating with layers of raw vermicelli broken to fit the dish, seasoning tomato layers with salt and pepper.
Heat lard or butter until boiling, pour over the tomatoes and vermicelli, and bake in the oven until the vermicelli is thoroughly done.
Allow to cool slightly before turning out onto a platter.

title: Macaroni "alla San Giovannello"
steps: Boil macaroni in salted water.
Chop ham fat fine with a little parsley.
Peel and slice tomatoes, removing seeds and hard parts.
Melt butter and chopped ham fat in a frying-pan, and when the grease is colored, add sliced tomatoes, salt, and pepper.
When the tomatoes are cooked and begin to sputter, add the boiled macaroni, mix well, stir in grated Parmesan cheese, and serve.

title: Ribbon Macaroni (Pasta fatta in Casa. Fettuccini)
steps: Place flour on a bread-board, make a well in the center, and add eggs, water, and salt.
Mix with a fork until flour is absorbed into a rollable paste.
Roll out very thin, about the thickness of a ten-cent piece, and let dry slightly.
Double over lengthwise multiple times and cut across into strips about half an inch wide.
Boil in two quarts of salted water for ten minutes and drain.
Serve with meat and sauce or tomato sauce and cheese.

title: Ravioli with Meat
ingredients: paste prepared as in ribbon macaroni recipe
tomato sauce or butter and grated Parmesan cheese
steps: Chop cooked meat very fine and mix in a bowl with grated Parmesan cheese, egg, nutmeg, lemon-peel, and cold butter.
Place teaspoonfuls of the mixture along the extended paste about two inches from the edge and two inches apart.
Fold the edge of the paste over the mixture, cut across at the bottom, and slice into individual squares with the meat in the center.
Press down the edges to seal.
Boil the squares in boiling salted water a few at a time for ten minutes.
Serve with tomato sauce or butter and grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Risotto with Ham
steps: Cut raw ham into small pieces and chop the onion fine.
Fry the ham, onion, and 1/2 tablespoon of butter slowly in a frying pan until golden.
Add uncooked rice and cook for a few minutes.
Add twice the rice's height in bouillon or water, salt, pepper, and a dash of nutmeg; mix well.
Boil over a good fire for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat, mix in 2 tablespoons of butter and grated Parmesan cheese, and serve.

title: Rice with Mushrooms
steps: Chop onion, parsley, celery, and carrot together and sauté in olive oil until colored.
Stir in tomato paste thinned with hot water, season with salt and pepper, and add chopped mushrooms.
Cook the sauce over medium heat for 20 minutes and set aside.
In a separate pan, fry the rice in a lump of butter until dry.
Add hot water gradually and boil gently.
When the rice is half cooked after about 10 minutes, stir in the prepared mushrooms and sauce.
Cook for another 10 minutes and top with grated Parmesan cheese before serving.

title: Polenta (Indian Meal)
steps: Put water into a granite or iron saucepan and add salt.
When boiling, add the Indian meal little by little while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Boil over a moderate fire for 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add a little more water if a thinner consistency is preferred.
Stir in grated cheese and butter before serving.

title: Polenta Fritters
steps: Bring milk with salt and sugar to a boil.
Pour in Indian meal gradually, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, and boil gently for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and beat in butter, egg yolk, and grated lemon-peel.
Turn mixture onto a dampened bread-board and spread to a finger's thickness to cool.
Cut into squares, diamonds, or rounds, dip in beaten egg, coat with bread crumbs, and fry a few at a time in boiling lard.
Sprinkle with sugar and serve hot.

title: Polenta "alla Toscana"
steps: Bring salted water to a boil, then add Indian meal gradually while stirring.
Boil over moderate heat for 30 minutes, stirring constantly until very stiff.
Dip a wooden spoon in hot water to loosen the polenta from the saucepan sides, then briefly hold the pan over high heat to release the bottom.
Turn the polenta out onto a bread-board to cool slightly in a mold.
Cut into finger-thick slices using a wire.
Layer the slices in a hot platter with meat gravy and grated cheese, repeating until all polenta is used.

title: Polenta with Chopped Sausages
ingredients: Indian meal (prepared as in preceding recipe)
steps: Prepare the Indian meal as directed in the preceding recipe.
Skin and finely chop the sausages, then fry them in butter until nicely browned.
Add stock and tomato paste thinned with hot water (or tomato sauce), and cook for 15 minutes.
Slice the polenta and layer it on a platter with the chopped sausages in sauce and grated cheese, just as before.

title: Chicken with Polenta
ingredients: ham fat (slice 4 fingers wide and 1 finger long) or 1 tablespoon lard
1 tablespoon tomato paste dissolved in a cup of hot water (or 1 cup tomato sauce)
steps: Clean and prepare the small chicken.
Chop the ham fat or lard very fine with half an onion, small carrot, and celery, and place in a saucepan.
Add the chicken, salt, pepper, and allspice, cover, and cook until browned on all sides, basting with the grease.
Add wine and let it absorb, then add tomato paste dissolved in hot water (or tomato sauce).
Simmer until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Prepare the Indian meal, surround it with the cooked chicken, pour the pan sauce over all, and sprinkle grated cheese over the Indian meal.

title: Polenta Pasticciata
ingredients: small piece of ham (fat and lean)
steps: Boil 1 quart of milk, add Indian meal gradually while stirring, cook for 30 minutes, add salt at the end, and turn out onto a bread-board to spread two fingers thick.

Make Meat Sauce: Dice the beef and ham; finely chop ham, onion, carrot, and celery. Brown meats and vegetables in 1 tablespoon butter, add a pinch of flour and bouillon gradually, and cook for 30 minutes without straining.
Make Béchamel Sauce: Brown 1 tablespoon flour and 1 tablespoon butter to a golden-brown, then slowly stir in 1 pint of milk until custard-like and white.
Cut the cooled polenta into 2-inch squares.
In a buttered baking dish, layer polenta squares, grated cheese, meat sauce, and Béchamel sauce, repeating layers and ending with Béchamel sauce on top.
Bake in a moderate oven until golden brown on top.

title: Polenta Cake (Migliaccio di Farina Gialla)
steps: Mix salt, sugar, raisins, and coarse Indian meal in a bowl.
Gradually pour in boiling water while stirring with a wooden spoon to form a stiff paste with no dry meal left at the bottom.
Grease a cake-tin with half of the lard.
Turn the Indian meal into the pan and smooth it out with the wooden spoon.
Spread the remaining softened lard over the top.
Bake in a slow oven until golden brown and serve hot.

title: Gnocchi of Farina (Gnocchi di Semolina)
steps: Bring milk to a boil with salt, then add farina gradually while stirring constantly.
Cook for 10 minutes while stirring.
Remove from heat and quickly beat in the egg before it sets.
Spread farina on a bread-board to the height of a finger, let it cool, and cut into 2-3 inch squares or diamonds.
Layer the squares in a well-buttered baking dish, sprinkling with grated cheese and dabs of butter between layers.
Finish with butter and cheese on top, and bake in a hot oven until a brown crust forms.

title: Gnocchi of Potato
steps: Boil potatoes in their skins, peel them when done, and pass through a fine colander.
Mix with salt and flour on a bread-board to form a dough.
Roll into a sausage shape three fingers thick and cut across into 1-inch pieces.
Press each piece lightly with a finger or knife handle to form little cup shapes.
Drop gnocchi into 2 quarts of boiling salted water; remove with a skimmer as they rise to the surface.
Transfer to a platter in batches, coating each layer well with gravy and cheese, and sprinkle grated cheese on top.

title: Gnocchi of Milk—a Dessert
steps: Mix milk, powdered starch, sugar, vanilla extract, and egg yolks in a saucepan.
Cook on the back of the stove over gentle heat until the mixture becomes stiff, stirring constantly.
Turn out onto a bread-board and spread to 1 1/2 fingers thick.
When cold, cut into diamonds or squares two fingers wide.
Arrange the squares overlapping in a buttered baking dish, dotting with butter between layers.
Brown in the oven.

title: Spinach Soufflé
ingredients: china cups or buttered papered forms
steps: Wash spinach in several waters and cook in a covered saucepan over a good fire, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 tablespoon of salt after 15 minutes, cook 5 more minutes, then drain and squeeze out the water.
Chop the spinach very fine.
Melt 1 generous tablespoon of butter in a saucepan with 3/4 tablespoon of flour, stir, and add half-cooked spinach, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 5 minutes, then add 4 to 5 tablespoons of cream while stirring constantly.
Take 1 cup of this prepared spinach, mix with the yolk of 1 egg, and stir over heat until the egg is set.
Allow to cool, then gently fold in the well-beaten whites of 3 eggs.
Fill china cups or buttered papered forms half full and bake in a hot oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Serve immediately.

title: Spinach "in Riccioli"
steps: Boil the spinach and pass it through a fine colander.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper, and mix in enough spinach to turn them green.
Heat a little olive-oil in a frying-pan (not boiling), pour in a small amount of the egg mixture, swirl the pan to make a very thin and dry pancake, and take it out. Repeat for the remaining egg.
Stack the pancakes, cut them into strips the width of a finger and about 2 inches long.
Fry the strips in butter and garnish with grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Spinach in a Mold with Mushrooms
ingredients: roux (made from 1 tablespoon of flour, 1 tablespoon of butter, and stock or milk)
steps: Boil spinach for a few moments, drain, squeeze out water, pound well, and pass through a fine colander.
Place spinach in a saucepan with a lump of butter and a few drops of lemon juice, boil briefly, turn into a dish, and let cool.
Mix beaten egg yolks into the cooled spinach.
Transfer to a buttered mold leaving a space in the middle, and bake in a slow oven for about an hour.
Prepare mushrooms by cooking them in a saucepan with butter, flour, salt, and pepper over a brisk fire for 10 minutes.
Moisten mushrooms with chicken broth or stock and add roux (cooked flour, butter, and stock or milk).
Stir in lemon juice, add the mushrooms and their sauce into the center of the unmolded spinach, and serve.

title: Flan of Vegetables
ingredients: vegetables (potato, spinach, carrot, small beet, etc.)
steps: Wash, finely chop, and boil the mixed vegetables, then boil them again in a saucepan with stock.
Add cream or milk, stir well, remove from heat, and let cool.
Stir in egg yolks, grated cheese, and beaten egg whites.
Transfer the mixture into a mold well buttered and lined with bread crumbs, and bake in the oven.

title: Lettuce in the Oven
steps: Wash young lettuces, remove wilted leaves, and tie their tops together.
Place side by side in a baking-pan, pour in 1 1/2 inches of stock, cover, and bake in a moderate oven for 30 minutes, adding stock as needed.
Lift each lettuce out with a fork, drain, and arrange doubled up on a hot dish.
Season the remaining pan gravy with butter, salt, and pepper, thicken with a beaten egg, and pour over the lettuce.

title: Cucumbers "alla Toscana"
steps: Peel and blanch cucumbers in boiling salted water for 5 minutes, drain, and cut into 1-inch thick pieces.
Place in a frying-pan with butter, a little flour, veal broth, salt, and pepper.
Reduce for about 15 minutes, stirring until boiling.
Stir in chopped parsley, grated nutmeg, cream, and beaten egg yolks.
Heat through for 3 to 4 minutes without boiling, and serve hot.

title: Cauliflower "in Stufato"
steps: Clean cauliflower, remove outer leaves, cut into pieces, wash in cold water, and boil in salted water for 20 to 30 minutes until tender.
Remove without breaking and place on pieces of buttered toast.
In a frying-pan, melt butter, add flour mixed with stock, stir until boiling, add chopped mushrooms, and cook briefly.
Remove from heat and stir in beaten egg yolks, salt, pepper, grated nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Pour sauce over and around the cauliflower without boiling it after adding the eggs.

title: Celery Fried
steps: Cut celery stalks into 1-inch pieces, wash, boil in water for 15 minutes, and dry on a napkin.
Beat an egg with stock or hot water, salt, and pepper.
Dip celery pieces into the egg mixture, roll in bread crumbs, and fry in boiling lard.

title: Celery with Tomato Sauce
ingredients: tomato sauce or tomato paste diluted with hot water
steps: Clean and wash celery stalks, boil fast in boiling water for 20 minutes.
Drain and dry well, place on a dish, and pour tomato sauce or diluted tomato paste over them.

title: Tomatoes "alla Piemontese"
steps: Boil unripe tomatoes in water for a few minutes.
Cut off stems, scoop out some of the inside and seeds.
Fill with boiled rice and chopped mushrooms.
Pour egg yolks over the tomatoes and bake in the oven to color. Serve hot.

title: Tomatoes "alla Spagnuola"
steps: Boil large ripe tomatoes, drain on a sieve, and pass through a fine hair-sieve.
Place the purée in a stew-pan and stir until all liquid evaporates.
Add a small piece of butter and raw eggs, stirring quickly.
When eggs are cooked, turn out into a dish and serve hot.

title: Tomatoes with Eggs
steps: Peel round tomatoes, cut off tops, and scoop out insides.
Drop a raw egg into each tomato and replace the top as a cover.
Bake in a baking-dish for about 10 minutes until eggs are set.
Serve very hot in the baking-dish with Béchamel sauce or brown gravy.

title: Tomato Pudding
steps: Scald, peel, and slice eight tomatoes.
Squeeze three-quarters of the juice through cheesecloth into a bowl and set aside.
Chop the tomato pulp with two tablespoons of bread crumbs, a little salt, sugar, pepper, and one tablespoon of melted butter.
Pour the mixture into a buttered mold, place in a double boiler, cover, and boil hard for one hour.
Turn the pudding out onto a dish.
Take the reserved tomato juice, season with sugar, salt, and pepper, and mix in one tablespoon of butter rolled in flour.
Boil for one minute, then pour over the pudding and serve.

title: String-beans "in Fricassea"
steps: Cut off ends and string young string-beans.
Cook in salted water with a pinch of soda to keep color, then drain well.
Place beans in a saucepan with butter, parsley, and chopped onion.
Add broth occasionally if the beans dry up before fully cooked.
Simmer slowly.
A few moments before removing from heat, stir in well-beaten egg yolks mixed with a little water, lemon juice, and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir occasionally, ensuring the mixture never boils or the eggs will set.

title: String-beans with Tomatoes
ingredients: juice of some tomatoes or good tomato conserve
steps: Cut off ends and string young string-beans, wash in cold water, and drain.
While still wet, place beans in a baking-dish with olive-oil, chopped onion, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Cover the dish and cook slowly on the fire.
As the beans dry, add tomato juice or tomato conserve, taking care they do not burn.

title: Fried Bread with Raisins
steps: Cut stale bread into slices, remove the crust, fry in lard, and arrange on a platter.
In a small saucepan, combine raisins, chopped raw ham, chopped sage leaf, granulated sugar, and vinegar.
Cook on the fire, stirring constantly until a syrup forms.
Pour the raisins onto the fried bread and the sauce over and around them.

title: Golden Bread
steps: Remove the crust from elastic bread and cut into slices about one inch thick, then cut into small pieces about three inches long and one inch wide, trimming neatly.
Place pieces in a bowl, pour boiling water over them, remove immediately, and plunge into cold water.
Gently squeeze out the water without breaking the pieces and place on a napkin to dry.
Dip in beaten egg seasoned with salt and pepper, allowing the egg to soak into the bread for fifteen minutes.
Heat a frying-pan with lard until lukewarm, add the bread pieces, and turn as they harden on one side.
Fry very slowly for at least ten minutes until golden and hollow inside.
Remove from lard, drain on a napkin, add a little salt, and serve very hot.

title: Sweetbreads
steps: Parboil the sweetbreads, then cook with butter and stock.
Cut cooked sweetbreads into smallish pieces.
Season with pepper, chopped parsley, and lemon juice.
Roll in flour, dip into beaten egg, and fry.

title: Fried Brains
steps: Soak the brain in cold water, changing the water periodically for a couple of hours until cleansed.
Transfer to another saucepan with fresh water, pieces of onion, salt, vinegar (one tablespoon per brain), and parsley stems.
Bring to a boil, immediately remove the saucepan from the heat, take out the brains, and place on a napkin.
Cut into four pieces, place on a plate, and season with a little olive-oil, lemon juice, and chopped parsley.
Roll in flour, dip in egg, and fry over a moderate fire for seven or eight minutes in olive-oil, lard, or butter.

title: Calf's Liver Fried
steps: Remove the skin from the liver and cut into large, thin slices.
Roll in flour, dip in egg, and fry in boiling lard for only a couple of minutes.
Drain on a napkin, sprinkle with a little salt, and serve.

title: Polenta Croquettes
steps: Boil corn-meal rather hard, adding butter and grated cheese before removing from fire, and mix well.
Drop by spoonfuls onto a marble-top table or a wetted bread-pan to form little balls the size of a hen's egg.
Place a very thin slice of Gruyère cheese on each croquette so it adheres to the corn-meal.
Allow to cool, then dip into beaten egg, roll in bread crumbs, and fry in boiling lard.

title: Egg Croquettes
steps: Hard boil two eggs, shell, dry, and chop into minute pieces.
Melt butter in a saucepan, add flour, and stir constantly over a slow fire without browning.
Pour in milk seasoned with salt and pepper, cook for eight to ten minutes stirring continually until smooth, then remove from heat.
Stir in the chopped eggs, finely chopped parsley, and grated Parmesan cheese.
Spread the mixture on a plate or marble surface to cool.
When cold and hardened, divide with a wooden spoon into portions the size of a nut.
Roll in dried bread crumbs and a little flour, shape into cork-like cylinders, dip in beaten egg, and roll in bread crumbs again.
Fry in boiling lard just before serving, removing immediately when colored to prevent breaking.

title: Little Filets "alla Napolitana"
steps: Butter a frying-pan and cover the bottom with finely chopped lean ham, chopped mushrooms, and minced parsley.
Cut round slices of beef filet about half an inch thick and arrange closely across the bottom of the pan.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and cook on the fire.
Turn the filets carefully when cooked on one side so the bottom ingredients stick to the meat.
Once cooked on both sides, squeeze lemon juice and add meat stock.
Transfer filets to a platter, pour the sauce over them, and serve with croutons (fried bread).

title: Involtini of Beef "alla Siciliana"
steps: Chop onion finely and sauté in a saucepan with butter or lard until colored.
Add parsley, chopped ham, small diced bread, salt, pepper, and a dash of nutmeg, mixing well.
Cut beef into six slices and pound to flatten; lightly salt.
Place a portion of the cooked mixture on each slice of meat.
Roll the meat like sausages and thread onto skewers, alternating with pieces of fried bread of the same size.
Butter well, roll in fresh bread crumbs, and broil on a gridiron over a slow fire.
Serve with salad.

title: Polpettone "alla Napolitana"
ingredients: three-quarters of a pound of lean beef rump-steak
one and one-half ounces of ham (fat and lean)
twice its volume of fresh bread crumbs
steps: Flatten the lean beef with a knife to widen it without tearing, and season with salt and pepper.
Chop finely the ham, a piece of onion, parsley, and thyme.
Mix the chopped mixture with fresh bread crumbs that have been dipped in water and squeezed out, then mix in the egg yolk.
Spread this mixture evenly over the beef, level with a knife, and sprinkle with raisins.
Roll up the meat like a cigar, thicker in the middle than the ends, and tie crosswise and lengthwise.
Brown the rolled meat in a saucepan with a little lard and some ham.
Add chopped onion, celery, carrot, and one clove as soon as it colors.
When the vegetables are cooked, add several pieces of tomato and let simmer for about two hours, basting occasionally.
Remove the string, place on a platter, strain the sauce through a sieve, pour over the meat, and serve.

title: Bocconcini
ingredients: meat (lamb, veal, mutton, or fresh pork)
steps: Cut meat into pieces about two inches wide, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Cut an equal number of bread pieces about one-half inch thick and slightly bigger than the meat.
Cut pieces of fat and lean ham the same size as the meat, using double the number.

Thread onto skewers: a piece of bread, a piece of ham, a sage leaf, a piece of meat, another sage leaf, ham, and bread, repeating so the meat sits between two sage leaves, two slices of ham, and two pieces of bread.
Coat everything well with olive-oil or melted butter, especially the bread.
Broil over a hot fire for about a quarter of an hour, turning constantly until golden brown and crisp, or cook in an oven in a pan.
Serve with lettuce salad.

title: Meat with Ribbon Macaroni
ingredients: three-quarters of a pound of meat (lamb, veal, beef, or fresh pork)
two tablespoons of red or white wine
one tablespoon of tomato paste or tomato sauce of fresh tomatoes
steps: Chop fine a piece of ham fat with a piece of onion, celery, and carrot, and place in a saucepan.
Cut the meat into several pieces, season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of allspice, and add to the saucepan.
Cook until well colored, then add red or white wine.
After the wine is absorbed, add tomato paste dissolved in water or fresh tomato sauce.
Cook over a moderate fire for one hour longer if veal or lamb, or one and a half to two hours for pork or beef, adding water if necessary.
Boil ribbon macaroni, mix with two tablespoons of grated Parmesan cheese, and arrange around the meat on a platter.
Pour sauce over all and sprinkle with a little more cheese before serving.

title: Salad "del Prevosto"
ingredients: one-half a glass of white wine
steps: Boil potatoes in their skins, peel, slice, and place in a salad bowl.
Pour white wine over the potatoes two or three hours before serving, mixing occasionally with a fork and spoon.
Shortly before the meal, add French salad dressing, cut pickled peppers, capers, and chopped parsley.
Mix well and serve.

title: The Cardinal's Salad
steps: Wash lettuce and water-cress.
Cut cold boiled beef into strips, add six radishes, chopped hard-boiled eggs, and sliced cucumber.
Mix these ingredients with sufficient mayonnaise sauce.
Arrange lettuce leaves in a salad bowl, place the mixture in the center, and serve.

title: Endive Salad
steps: Wash and dry a head of endive, and place in a salad bowl.
Pour olive-oil over the endive.
Mix honey or sugar, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a cup, and pour over the salad just before serving.

title: Italian Salad
steps: Slice carrot and turnip and cook in boiling soup; let cool.
Mix the cooked vegetables with cold boiled potatoes and beet cut into strips.
Add a little chopped leeks or onion.
Pour sauce "Lombarda" over the salad and garnish with water-cress.

title: "Alla Pollastra" Salad
steps: Chop lettuce leaves and celery, and cut the leftover cold fowl into small pieces.
Mix in a salad bowl with vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Pour a cup of mayonnaise sauce over the top.
Garnish with quarters of hard-boiled egg, capers, stoned olives, and small tender lettuce leaves.

title: "Alla Macedoine" Salad
ingredients: two tablespoons of cold cooked peas
steps: Cut cold boiled beet and half an onion into small pieces.
Combine with cold boiled string-beans, asparagus tips, peas, boiled carrot, and celery.
Mix together, pour mayonnaise sauce over all, add lemon juice, and serve.

title: Chestnut Fritters
ingredients: one level tablespoon of powdered sugar
steps: Roast chestnuts on a slow fire without coloring, remove shells without breaking the nuts.
Simmer chestnuts in a saucepan with powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla for over half an hour.
Drain and pass the chestnuts through a sieve.
Mix with butter and egg yolks without cooking; let cool.
Shape small portions (nut-sized), dip in egg and bread crumbs, and fry in butter and lard a few at a time.
Serve hot dusted with powdered sugar.

title: Chestnuts "alla Lucifero"
ingredients: two or three tablespoons of powdered sugar
steps: Roast chestnuts over a slow fire without drying or coloring them, then carefully remove the shells.
Place chestnuts in a bowl and pour rum and powdered sugar over them.
Set fire to the rum and baste the chestnuts constantly while burning, turning them to absorb the rum and become colored.

title: Peaches with Wine
ingredients: piece of a rind of lemon
steps: Halve, stone, peel, and thinly slice ripe peaches into a bowl, covering until ready.
Boil red wine, powdered sugar, cinnamon, and lemon rind together in a saucepan.
Pour the boiling liquid over the peaches, cover, and let stand for at least two hours before serving.
